newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac weighing election intervention.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac weighing election intervention.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac is weighing another intervention in France's parliamentary election campaign but may wait until after next Sunday's first round of voting before addressing the nation, a close aide said on Monday.

Francois Baroin, one of Chirac's speechwriters and political advisers, told Europe 1 radio that the president would make up his mind after returning early on Monday from a state visit to China and a stopover in Moscow.

"It's up to him to decide whether or not to intervene, whether a bit more explanation is needed or whether he should reserve that possibility for after the results of the first message the French people will give next Sunday," Baroin said.
He played down widely-reported rumours that Chirac might speak at an election rally later this week alongside leaders of his centre-right coalition.
"If you ask my opinion, I am against the principle of a rally. He is the president of all the French people and he should not get involved alongside others.
"He should simply set the course...and play his role as arbiter while saying what is good and right for the country," said Baroin, Chirac's 1995 presidential campaign spokesman.
The aide, who was the first to launch the idea that Chirac might dismiss unpopular Prime Minister Alain Juppe, said the president had a free choice of options for weighing on the election campaign.
"He can intervene before the first round. He can intervene before the (June 1) second round. He can do both. Or he might not intervene at all," he said.
Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin has said he would demand a right of reply if Chirac broadcast to the nation just before the first round of voting.

Opinion polls published before a legal blackout at midnight on Saturday showed the centre-right clinging to a reduced lead of between 39 and 100 seats in the 577-member National Assembly with the leftwing opposition almost level in voting intentions.
